calls.head: The Lightning should tilt the ice
calls.body: The Lightning have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Predators near the bottom. Expect the Lightning to spend more of the night in the Predators’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Stamkos seals it in the shootout
paras: Reid Schaefer got the scoring started for the Predators midway through the first, but John Carlson tied it up for Tampa Bay less than three minutes later. It was a busy second period. Jake Guentzel gave the Lightning the lead just 18 seconds into the period, but Adam Edström made it 2-2 for Nashville just 45 seconds into the period. Victor Hedman put the Lightning back ahead 3-2 less than three minutes later. Jayden Struble tied it 3-3 for Nashville with 18 seconds left in the second, and Conor Geekie restored the Lightning’s lead early in the third. Steven Stamkos tied it 4-4 for Nashville on the power play just under four minutes later. Stamkos scored the only goal of the shootout for the Predators. The Lightning’s Nikita Kucherov finished with three assists.

The Predators had the better of the chances, outshooting the Lightning 33-26. Justus Annunen made 22 saves for the Predators, and Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 29 of 33 at the other end. The Predators moved to 5-4-5, sixth in the Central, while the Bolts fell to 8-3-2, fourth in the Atlantic.

items.text: Ryan O'Reilly has a point in five straight games.
Reid Schaefer scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 26 (16 games played since).
The Predators bounced back after two straight losses.
NHL.com had projected the Lightning with 11 forwards and seven defensemen, but they dressed 12 and six.
